articles.title: The Batman Part 2 to Resume Filming With New Director
articles.summary: Steven Soderbergh is stepping in to help complete The Batman Part 2, starring Robert Pattinson, as questions remain about the DC sequel's release date
body: Steven Soderbergh is stepping in to help finish filming The Batman Part 2 while director Matt Reeves attends to an ongoing family matter.

According to Deadline, the Oscar-winning filmmaker will help complete the final weeks of principal photography on the DC sequel. Reeves will remain in communication with Soderbergh throughout the process, working closely with him to ensure the footage aligns with his vision. Reeves is expected to take over post-production when he is ready to return.
Soderbergh, known for films including Ocean's Eleven and Traffic, volunteered to help after expressing his admiration for Reeves' work on 2022's The Batman.

“I thought Matt Reeves’ work on The Batman was stunning; it was intentional, specific, and rigorously coherent,” Soderbergh said in a statement. “The goal here is to work with Matt and his team to generate footage that will integrate seamlessly with what’s already been shot so Matt can properly finish his film.”

articles.title: 'I Just Sort of Disconnect' — Jeff Kaplan is Avoiding Overwatch at all Costs
articles.summary: Former Overwatch director Jeff Kaplan explained how he protects his psyche by completely avoiding online discussions and subreddits about Blizzard's hero shooter. If you’re a die-hard Overwatch player, you’re likely familiar with the name Jeff Kaplan.
body: After leaving Blizzard in 2021, Kaplan founded his own game development studio and is currently working on an open world, action-survival shooter called The Legend of California. He has firmly put Overwatch behind him — to the point where he avoids interacting with it at all costs online.
“With Overwatch, I had a very almost clinical separation, knowing how the WoW thing had gone,” Kaplan said in a recent interview with GameSpot. “I’ve literally not played the game since April 2021.

He told the outlet that it was surprisingly more painful for him to leave the World of Warcraft team to work on Overwatch than it was to put the hero shooter in his rear view, calling it a “training moment” for taking the next step in his career.

articles.title: Why Rockstar Canceled Its PlayStation-Exclusive Follow-Up To GTA 4
articles.summary: At E3 2009, Sony announced that it was partnering with Rockstar on a PlayStation-exclusive spy game called Agent, with Rockstar founders Sam and Dan Houser overseeing development. The game never materialized, though, and now Dan Houser has shared more details as to why.
body: Speaking to IGN, Houser said Agent never coming out shouldn't be a total shock because he worked on "a bunch of games that never came out." He said Rockstar tried with two or three different teams to make Agent--an open-world spy game--but the teams just "could not get it right."
"And it never came out. We concluded that it was not a game we were ever going to figure out how to make. Other people can try, but I personally think it's hard," he said.
Great spy movies like the James Bond series work so well because they take viewers all over the world, but "that's not an experience in an open-world game that really works," Houser said.
"So we tried lots of things and couldn't get it quite right," Houser said, going on to say that the teams built great elements but they never came together in a full package.

articles.title: Rep. Ritchie Torres Introduces Legislation to Ensure Gamers Own Their Digital Games
articles.summary: Democratic Congressman Ritchie Torres is introducing legislation that aims to ensure you own your digital games, rather than merely buying a license that gives you permission to play them.
body: The bill, known as The Power to the Players Act, would direct the Fedral Trade Commission (FTC) to establish regulations that would protect gamers and their digital libraries. In short, Torres wants to ensure that when you buy a digital game, you actually own it, as opposed to getting a license that can be revoked. Additionally, the bill would require online games to have offline functionality, so that when servers are shut down, the content can still be played by those who own the game.

“Consumers must have the right to own, the right to play, and the right to transfer the games they buy,” Torres said in a press release. “A game that can be taken away the moment a company pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale. Families in the Bronx and across the country save up to buy these games, and they deserve better than a license that can vanish at any time. The Power To The Players Act ensures consumers own what they buy and can keep playing long after a company moves on.”

articles.title: Call Of Duty: MW4 Is Not On Xbox Game Pass, But Here’s When You Can Expect It
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is set for release on October 23, and in a big shakeup, it will not be available on Xbox Game Pass at launch. This has been known for a while, but Activision is reminding people of this in a new blog post on the eve of the game's campaign early access on October 16.
body: Upon release, the only way to get MW4 is by purchasing it outright, starting at $70 for the base edition and scaling to $100 for the Vault edition.
Activision said MW4 will be available on Xbox Game Pass at some point at the end of next year, meaning it will be "windowed" as a standalone purchase for about one year.

2024’s Black Ops 6 was the first entry in the series to launch directly into Xbox Game Pass, with Black Ops 7 following the same playbook in 2025. However, Microsoft announced earlier this year that new Call of Duty titles would no longer debut in Game Pass, an announcement it made in conjunction with a price cut for the subscription service.

Microsoft has never explicitly said why it made this major change, but it could have to do with lost sales. It was reported that Black Ops 6 coming to Game Pass in 2024 amounted to Microsoft missing out on hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue. That number has been debated, and it does not tell the whole story, but no doubt there was a financial impact that Microsoft is responding to.
points: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is set for release on October 23, and in a big shakeup, it will not be available on Xbox Game Pass at launch.

body: Not just any ridiculously oversized tie, however. People who preorder First Light for Switch 2 get the GoldenEye Suit, and it includes the suit and tie that Pierce Brosnan wore in the famous 1995 movie, including the oversized tie.
Brosnan wore a lot of suits in that movie, but the one being referenced here is the one with the oversized tie, which was the style at the time.

GoldenEye has a special history with Nintendo specifically, which may help explain why Switch 2 owners are getting this outfit and no one else is. After all, 1997's GoldenEye 007, which was based on the movie, is one of the most iconic N64 games of all time.
First Light has been a big hit, critically and commercially, scoring great reviews and selling more than 4 million copies, and that's before the Switch 2 version even comes out.

body: Viewers of the GTA 6 Extended Look might have been snickering every time protagonists Jason and Lucia uttered the word "Boobie," but the official GTA 6 website indicates that the character of Boobie Ike is a Vice City powerhouse. Though he's implied to be a highly influential figure in the game's story, he hasn't made an appearance in any trailers.

Boobie is the owner of the Jack of Hearts club, seen in the extended look trailer. His "legitimate empire" also includes real estate investments and a recording studio, and in his words, "the drug money pay for it all." The first segment of the extended look video has Jason and Lucia making a pickup on behalf of Boobie, and simply saying his name was enough to grant them access.

The lack of Boobie in any GTA 6 trailers does prompt curiosity about his larger role in the story. It has already been the subject of speculation in social media posts and YouTube videos, with some predicting that he'll turn out to be an antagonist who double-crosses Jason and Lucia. It's also possible that Boobie's presence in the story will be by name only, as he pulls strings from the background.

articles.title: How to unlock fast travel in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse
articles.summary: Fast travel is tucked away until you make a fair amount of progress in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse. If you want to revisit old haunts in the early game and uncover treasures you missed, you'll have to go on foot — or just hold off for a couple of hours.
body: Below, we explain when you unlock fast travel in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse and how it works.

Fast travel unlocks automatically when you meet the Boatman, though that won't happen for a while. The door that takes you to one of his ferry stops is tucked away deep in the Catacombs. You can only access the catacombs after defeating three bosses around Paris — Medusa, Joan at the top of Prison Tower, and The Fallen — and obtaining their emblems.

Vast and imposing as the catacombs are, there's only one way down. Follow the path into the depths, using the green wall markers as a guide if you ever get turned around or lose your way. Make sure to open the pathways back to the mirror room as you descend, so you can quickly return to and from the depths via elevator.

articles.title: US lawmaker calls videogame purchases rentals disguised as sales: 'When you pay for a game, you should own it'
articles.summary: US Representative Ritchie Torres, a Democrat from New York City, announced today that he will introduce the "Power To The Players Act." If it becomes law, the bill will see the US Federal Trade Commission create regulations that protect our "ability to own and play" purchased games, according to…
body: "When you pay for a game, you should own it," says Torres. "Consumers must have the right to own, the right to play, and the right to transfer the games they buy. A game that can be taken away the moment a company pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale."

The game ownership issue is longstanding on PC, which moved to digital distribution a couple decades ago, but has recently come to the foreground of public consciousness as the consoles also transition away from discs. Earlier this year, Sony announced that it will end physical disc production in 2028.

The related problem of online games being decommissioned before players are done with them has also received more attention in recent years. The Stop Killing Games campaign in particular has raised the issue's profile, arguing that basic offline functionality should be expected when online games are retired. Founder Ross Scott and organizer Moritz Katzner gained an audience with the European Parliament earlier this year.
points: US Representative Ritchie Torres, a Democrat from New York City, announced today that he will introduce the "Power To The Players Act.

articles.title: Steam achievements are getting a huge overhaul, with separate sets for DLC and season passes, and an easy way to compare with friends
articles.summary: Valve has pushed a new update to its Steam client beta introducing big changes to how achievements work and how they're displayed. Developers can now create sets of achievements customized to their game, like mastering a specific character class or finishing a singleplayer campaign.
body: Previously if you unlocked all achievements for a game you'd see a nice 'n' tidy 100% in your achievements list. But if that game got DLC with new achievements, that 100% would drop accordingly. I can understand why achievement heads would be annoyed by this: what if you have no intention of playing the DLC, but want to retain 100% completion bragging rights? This update fixes that, assuming devs use it.

It's a similar situation for seasonal achievements, which I can see working well with battle passes. The example Valve uses is a set called "Halloween Event Achievements" which are valid for a certain period and don't affect the achievement count of the base game. In other words: if you have the completionist itch but skip a season, it won't affect your base game stats.

All these changes have prompted a refresh of the achievements page. Most achievements info is now displayed on a single page: your progress towards overall completion, and your progress towards unlocking individual achievements.
points: Valve has pushed a new update to its Steam client beta introducing big changes to how achievements work and how they're displayed.
Developers can now create sets of achievements customized to their game, like mastering a specific character class or finishing a singleplayer campaign.

articles.title: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave gets its first wave of DLC today, and an expansion pass to include it
articles.summary: Nintendo and Intelligent Systems have released an expansion pass for Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, introducing a string of DLC additions to the tactical RPG starting today, and through into 2027.
body: The expansion pass, which can be bought on the Nintendo eShop for $34.99 / £29.99, comes in three parts. For those who buy it now, a selection of weapons are made available to use within the game. The second part of the expansion pass arrives this holiday season, and the final part arrives in 2027.
We already know a bit about what's coming in these latter DLC releases. The second portion features additional outfits for the game's cast, alongside three new allies: Aurora, Smyrnos, and Jurah.

The final segment of the pass looks to be the most substantial; introducing new stories to play, new allies, classes, and additional goodies. Those new stories make an already chunky game even larger, something that should give people a reason to go back to the RPG next year, and those yet to pick up the game, a convenient jumping-on point.

Fortune's Weave has been met with critical acclaim and sizable early sales figures. In Eurogamer's review, the game is described as "a synergy of everything that has made the series great for generations", and "a sumptuous feast of a game".
points: Nintendo and Intelligent Systems have released an expansion pass for Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, introducing a string of DLC additions to the tactical RPG starting today, and through into 2027.

body: Castlevania's Belmont's Curse revives the legendary 2D series with striking visuals, a distinctive soundtrack, solid combat and excellent exploration. It's not as break-through as some other recent Metroidvanias, but it nails the fundamentals in a way that's sure to satisfy fans of the genre.
